disputed_statements.label: D
disputed_statements.text: has numerous deep papillae in the alveolar mucosa

proposed_interpretation: The normal alveolar lining mucosa generally shows sparse, short connective tissue papillae. A false mark for this statement warrants lecturer consideration.
reason: Human alveolar mucosa examined by electron microscopy showed occasional short, slender papillae. Attached gingiva is a separate tissue with more pronounced interdigitation. The existing note attributes a contrary regional exception to an unavailable lecture. The general statement about fewer, shorter papillae remains consistent with the teaching sources.
sources: Quantitative electron microscopic analysis of the epithelium of normal human alveolar mucosa, PMID 872202, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/872202/
Architecture and density of the connective tissue papillae of the human oral mucosa, PMID 838625, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/838625/
Manual of Oral Histology and Oral Pathology, nonkeratinized mucosa and gingiva, https://cbspd.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/assets/documents/9789354660603S.pdf
ask_lecturer: Can you provide the teaching slide and confirm whether the intended site was alveolar lining mucosa or attached gingiva?

stem: Swell bodies of the nasal conchae perform all of the following EXCEPT:

options.label: B
options.text: Adjustment of the temperature of inspired air

options.label: C
options.text: Regulation of blood flow to the overlying epithelium

options.label: D
options.text: Increasing contact between inspired air and the nasal mucosa

options.label: E
options.text: Increasing pressure in the nasal cavity

disputed_statements.label: E
disputed_statements.text: Increasing pressure in the nasal cavity

proposed_interpretation: Sensory perception is not a function of the vascular swell bodies. Raising nasal cavity pressure is also a questionable function as written.
reason: Engorgement changes airway calibre and resistance, increasing the pressure difference required to maintain a given flow. That differs from increasing pressure throughout the nasal cavity. More than one exclusion is defensible.
sources: Physiology, Nasal, nasal cycle and resistance, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK526086/
ask_lecturer: Was increased resistance or the pressure gradient across the nose intended by “increasing pressure in the nasal cavity”?

proposed_interpretation: The respiratory lining and position identify the vestibular folds, but absence of muscle is too absolute in humans.
reason: Anatomical sections of human vestibular folds show variable striated muscle bundles. The characteristic vocalis muscle of a true vocal fold is a different feature.
sources: Amount and spatial arrangement of muscle fibers in the human laryngeal Musculus ventricularis, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37092576/

proposed_interpretation: Type I and II pneumocytes are well established; whether occasional brush cells should be taught as normal human alveolar lining cells needs confirmation.
reason: Some clinical teaching sources include brush cells in alveoli. A species-specific review distinguishes reported rat alveolar brush cells from normal human alveoli. The choice gives no species qualifier.
sources: Keeping it together: Pulmonary alveoli are maintained by a hierarchy of cellular programs, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5679707/
